div.head: CHn cor 11
div.ab: Militibus qui per loricas terras suas deseruiunt terras dominicarum carrucarum suarum quietas ab omnibus geldis et ab omni opere, proprio dono meo, concedo, ut, sicut tam magno gravamine alleviati sunt, ita equis et armis se bene instruant, ut apti et parati sint ad seruitium meum et ad defensionem regni mei.

Militibus, qui per loricas terras suas defendunt, terras dominicarum carrucarum suarum quietas ab omnibus gildis et omni opere proprio dono meo concedo, ut, sicut tam magno [gravamine] alleviati sunt, ita equis et armis se bene instruant, ut apti et parati sint ad servitium meum et ad defensionem regni mei.

To knights who hold their lands by military service I grant, by my own gift, that the lands which they hold in demesne shall be free from all payments and from all labour services, so that, as the result of being freed from so great a burden, they may equip themselves fittingly with horses and arms in order to be prepared and ready for service to me and for the defence of my realm.

Vgl. Gl Lehnwesen 10b. c. Zunächst werden nur Kronritter befreit (servitium meum; vgl. Gl Vassallität 2); die mittelbaren Ritter, Aftervassallen, sind gemeint nur insofern, als deren Herr gelda et opus für den Staat ihnen nur soweit auferlegen durfte, als er sie selbst verantworten musste; vgl. 2, 1. 4, 2

Cf. Gl Lehnwesen 10b. c. In the first place only the Crown’s knights are exempted (servitium meum; cf. Gl Vassallität 2); the mediate knights, the sub-vassals, are meant only in so far as their lord was allowed to impose gelda et opus for the state on them only to the extent that he himself had to answer for them; cf. 2, 1. 4, 2

per armorum servicia (per arma et hernesia, per plena arma) feudum suum deservire (‘verdienen’) gewohnte Phrase; z. B. terras de abbate (als dem Lehnsherrn) deservire; Hist. Eli. 260; vgl. Summa de leg. Norm. 85, 10. Die Stelle ist auch sonst mit Normann. Rechtssprache verwandt; z. B. Anglorum temporibus . . in Normannia . . omnes feodum lorice possidentes equum et arma habere tenebantur, . . ut prompti (s. Variante 46) et apparati ad mandatum principis invenirentur; Summa leg. Norm. retr. 22 bis 9.—Nur das inland (im Ggs. zu warland, terra geldabilis) des Lehns wird hiernach frei von Steuer; s. d. Gl 7b [so auch Vinogradoff in Law Quart. rev. 21 (1905) 251]; und Wl art retr 8{m}.—Die Worte{39} defendunt et, omnino{42} und{48} sicut—fideliores sint et fügt ein auch Rs

per armorum servicia (per arma et hernesia, per plena arma) feudum suum deservire (‘to earn’) is a customary phrase; e.g. terras de abbate (as the feudal lord) deservire; Hist. Eli. 260; cf. Summa de leg. Norm. 85, 10. The passage is related to Norman legal language in other respects too; e.g. Anglorum temporibus . . in Normannia . . omnes feodum lorice possidentes equum et arma habere tenebantur, . . ut prompti (see variant 46) et apparati ad mandatum principis invenirentur; Summa leg. Norm. retr. 22 bis 9.—Accordingly only the inland (in contrast to warland, terra geldabilis) of the fief becomes free of tax; see that word in Gl 7b [so too Vinogradoff in Law Quart. rev. 21 (1905) 251]; and Wl art retr 8{m}.—The words{39} defendunt et, omnino{42} and{48} sicut—fideliores sint et are also inserted by Rs

‘Danegeld and special services of castle guard and the like’ versteht Stubbs (Lect. 119), proprio richtig von opere trennend; die Trinoda necessitas versteht unter opus Robertson Hist. essays XVII; Hn meint m. E. beides

Stubbs (Lect. 119) understands ‘Danegeld and special services of castle guard and the like’, rightly separating proprio from opere; Robertson Hist. essays XVII understands opus as the trinoda necessitas; in my opinion Hn means both
Die Zufügung des Q zeigt dessen Stil; vgl. Wb: propensus, benignitas
The addition by Q shows his style; cf. Wb: propensus, benignitas
S. o. {a}.—Da Heinrich die Normandie noch nicht besass, vielleicht noch nicht erstrebte, fehlt hier der Dienst ausserhalb Englands; s. o. S. 280 zu Wl art 2{c}
See above {a}.—Since Henry did not yet possess Normandy, and perhaps did not yet aspire to it, service outside England is not mentioned here; see above p. 280 on Wl art 2{c}
